taxonomyNote: Cynomys parvidens (Utah prairie dog) has been regarded by some authors as a subspecies; NatureServe cites Thorington and Hoffmann (2005) recognizing it as separate.
fieldMarks: Gray to yellowish-brown upper body with dark cheek patches / dark patches above and below each eye
Whitish to grayish tip on the short tail
Head and body 342-399 mm in males, 315-375 mm in females
Usually at higher elevation than black-tailed prairie dogs
behavior: Loosely colonial; alarm 'repetitious bark', 'laughing bark' for group cohesion, snarl and growl
Feeds mainly on forbs and grasses
Hibernates; emerges from late February-March, males 2-3 weeks before females; by late August all adults are inactive
Morning and late-afternoon activity in summer
habitat: Open shrublands, semidesert grasslands and open valleys at 5,000-10,000 ft; sage is important cover.
range: From the Bighorn Basin in southern Montana across central and southwestern Wyoming into western and north-central Colorado and eastern Utah.

lookalikes.howToTell: Black-tipped tail and a lower-elevation, grassland habitat.
